headline: Historic win: Bangladesh beat Australia in Darwin for first-ever Test win on their soil
summary: The Tigers crushed Australia by nine wickets, becoming the quickest Asian team to win a Test in Australia.
details: Bangladesh achieved a historic milestone in Darwin, defeating Australia by nine wickets on Sunday. This marks the Tigers' first-ever Test victory on Australian soil, ending a 23-year wait.
The Tigers bowled the hosts out for 284 before chasing a target of 57 with ease, wrapping up the match in the second session of Day 4.
Bangladesh is now the quickest Asian team to win a Test in Australia, achieving the feat in their third Test Down Under, ahead of Pakistan (7) and India (12).
Australia has not lost a home Test to an Asian team other than India since 1995, 31 years ago.
Hasan Mahmud delivered a standout performance, taking 9-111 in the match. These are the best match figures by a Bangladesh bowler outside the country.
Tanzid Tamim became the sixth Bangladesh player to score both a century and a duck in the same Test match.
Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto recorded his third away Test win, the most by any Bangladesh captain, and now holds the record for most Test wins overall as captain (9).
The victory was celebrated by a record-breaking crowd of 18,352 fans who attended the Darwin Test.

Australia has not lost a home Test to an Asian team other than India since 1995, 31 years ago.

Hasan Mahmud delivered a standout performance, taking 9-111 in the match. These are the best match figures by a Bangladesh bowler outside the country.

Tanzid Tamim became the sixth Bangladesh player to score both a century and a duck in the same Test match.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto recorded his third away Test win, the most by any Bangladesh captain, and now holds the record for most Test wins overall as captain (9).

The victory was celebrated by a record-breaking crowd of 18,352 fans who attended the Darwin Test.

headline: 11 dead as boat drifts for 11 days in Mediterranean
summary: A survivor reports that nine Bangladeshis died after their Greece-bound boat broke down, leaving 42 passengers adrift without food or water.
details: At least 11 passengers, including nine Bangladeshis, died after a boat carrying 42 people drifted for 11 days in the Mediterranean Sea without food or water.

A survivor, Abdul Karim of Sunamganj, stated that the boat's engine broke down as they approached Greece, leaving them stranded. He reported that the bodies of those who died were thrown into the sea.
The boat eventually reached the Marsa Matruh coast of Egypt on August 13, where approximately 30 survivors were rescued by local police and taken to hospitals.
The boat, which had a capacity of only 25 people, was overloaded with 42 passengers, including 38 Bangladeshis and four Sudanese.
The Bangladesh Embassy in Cairo has sought consular access to the survivors to verify the details, as Egyptian police have not yet confirmed the deaths.
Data from Frontex cited by Brac reveals that Bangladeshis are now the top nationality reaching Greece by sea from Libya, with 3,608 making the journey between January and June this year.
This tragedy follows a similar incident in March where at least 18 Bangladeshis died while traveling from Libya to Greece, including 12 from Sunamganj.

Shariful Hasan of Brac warned that the high number of migrants crossing the Mediterranean is damaging the country's international image and urged government agencies to work together to stop human trafficking.
